script: Around 300 million years ago, dragonfly-like insects had wings as wide as a hawk's. One, called Meganeura, had a wingspan of about 70 centimeters. This was long before the dinosaurs, in the Carboniferous period. The air then held more oxygen than today, which may have helped insects grow big. A millipede relative called Arthropleura grew over 2 meters long. Much of the coal burned today formed from the swampy forests of that time. Follow DinoBytes for more prehistoric facts.
